In recent discussions on social media, a claim has circulated stating that the number of deaths in May 2021 remained stable when compared to May 2019. This assertion has garnered attention due to ongoing debates about the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and related public health measures. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine the available mortality data, consider the context of both years, and analyze potential contributing factors.

May 2019 was a pre-pandemic period characterized by typical seasonal mortality trends. Death rates during this time were influenced primarily by established patterns such as age demographics, chronic health conditions, accidents, and other non-pandemic-related causes. By comparison, May 2021 occurred more than a year into the global COVID-19 pandemic, a period marked by waves of viral transmission, ongoing vaccination campaigns, and varying degrees of public health restrictions.

At the onset of the pandemic in 2020, many countries experienced substantial increases in mortality, particularly during peak infection waves. However, by May 2021, several factors contributed to changing death patterns. Vaccination programs were underway in many regions, targeting high-risk populations and resulting in a decline in COVID-19-related mortality. Additionally, improvements in medical treatments, public awareness, and adaptations in healthcare delivery helped mitigate the impact of the virus.

Analyzing official mortality statistics from relevant national agencies for May 2019 and May 2021 reveals nuanced trends. In some countries, the number of recorded deaths in May 2021 was indeed comparable to, or only marginally higher than, the figures from May 2019. This stability can be attributed to the effectiveness of interventions and the seasonal lull in respiratory infections, which typically occurs in late spring. For instance, regions with successful vaccination rollouts and lower transmission rates reported mortality numbers that closely matched pre-pandemic levels.

However, it is important to note that the situation varied across different locations. Some areas continued to experience elevated death rates due to ongoing outbreaks, healthcare disruptions, or indirect effects of the pandemic, such as delayed medical care for non-COVID conditions. These disparities reflect the complexity of monitoring and interpreting mortality trends during a global health crisis.

Another consideration is that excess mortality—the number of deaths above what would be expected based on historical averages—provides a more comprehensive measure of the pandemic's impact. While some countries saw excess deaths subside to near-normal levels by May 2021, others faced lingering challenges.

In summary, the claim that the number of deaths in May 2021 remained stable when compared to May 2019 is accurate in many contexts, especially in regions where vaccination and public health measures were effective. Nevertheless, the overall picture is multifaceted, with some areas experiencing continued elevated mortality. As with all statistical comparisons, it is essential to account for local conditions, demographic changes, and the broader effects of the pandemic to fully understand the data.

A widely shared social media post claims that COVID-19 cases in India sharply declined after the government halted its vaccination campaign and instead distributed ivermectin, allowing the reopening of the Taj Mahal for visitors. This article examines the accuracy of these claims, providing context and fact-based analysis.

The core assertion is threefold: first, that India stopped vaccinating its population; second, that ivermectin was widely adopted as a replacement treatment; and third, that these actions led to a dramatic drop in COVID-19 cases, enabling the reopening of major tourist sites like the Taj Mahal.

India’s COVID-19 Response: Vaccines and Treatment

India faced a devastating second wave of COVID-19 in the spring of 2021, with daily cases peaking above 400,000. In response, the government ramped up its vaccination drive, using vaccines such as Covishield and Covaxin. At no point did the Indian government officially stop its vaccination campaign. In fact, the national vaccination program continued to be a central pillar of India’s COVID-19 response, with eligibility expanding over time to include all adults and, later, teenagers. As of 2024, India has administered over 2.2 billion vaccine doses.

Ivermectin and Official Guidelines

Amid the crisis, some Indian states, notably Uttar Pradesh and Goa, did include ivermectin in their local COVID-19 treatment protocols. Ivermectin is a medication primarily used to treat parasitic infections, and early in the pandemic, it was investigated as a possible treatment for COVID-19. However, major health agencies, including the World Health Organization, later advised against its use for COVID-19 outside of clinical trials due to insufficient evidence. India’s national guidelines evolved in time, with ivermectin eventually removed from the recommended treatment list. There is no evidence that the central government replaced vaccination with ivermectin as the main strategy.

COVID-19 Cases and Reopening of the Taj Mahal

The post claims that cases “plummeted” after these supposed policy changes, allowing the Taj Mahal to reopen. While it is true that after the deadly second wave, COVID-19 cases in India dropped sharply by late June and July 2021, this decline coincided with a dramatic increase in vaccinations, continued mask mandates, and the imposition of local restrictions. The reopening of the Taj Mahal and other tourist sites was tied to the decrease in cases and the broader relaxation of lockdown measures, not to the cessation of vaccination or the exclusive use of ivermectin.

Conclusion

The claim that India stopped vaccinating its population and instead relied on ivermectin, leading to a sharp decline in COVID-19 cases and the reopening of the Taj Mahal, is not supported by the evidence. India’s vaccination campaign continued throughout the pandemic and was instrumental in controlling subsequent waves. Ivermectin was used in limited contexts but was not a national replacement for vaccines. The reopening of tourist sites was a result of falling case numbers, which were influenced by multiple public health measures, not by the abandonment of vaccination in favor of ivermectin.

В данной статье рассматриваются достоверность этих заявлений, а также приводится контекст и анализ на основе фактов.

Основное утверждение состоит из трех пунктов: в первую очередь, что Индия прекратила вакцинацию населения; во-вторых, что ивермектин широко использовался как альтернативное лечение; и, наконец, что эти действия привели к резкому падению случаев заболевания COVID-19, что позволило открыть крупные туристические достопримечательности, такие как Тадж-Махал.

Ответ Индии на пандемию: вакцины и лечение

Весной 2021 года Индия столкнулась с разрушительной второй волной заболевания, при этом ежедневные случаи превышали 400 000. В ответ правительство усилило свою вакцинационную кампанию, используя вакцины, такие как Covishield и Covaxin. В какой-либо момент правительство Индии официально не прекращало свою вакцинационную кампанию. На самом деле, национальная вакцинационная программа оставалась центральным элементом ответа Индии на пандемию, и постепенно критерии вакцинации расширялись, чтобы включить всех взрослых, а позже и подростков. К 2024 году в Индии было введено более 2,2 миллиарда доз вакцин.

Ивермектин и официальные рекомендации

В условиях кризиса некоторые штаты Индии, в частности Уттар-Прадеш и Гоа, включили ивермектин в местные протоколы лечения от COVID-19. Ивермектин — это лекарство, в основном используемое для лечения паразитарных инфекций, и на ранних этапах пандемии его рассматривали как возможное средство для лечения COVID-19. Однако крупные международные организации здравоохранения, включая Всемирную организацию здравоохранения, позже рекомендовали использовать ивермектин для лечения COVID-19 только в клинических испытаниях из-за недостатка доказательств эффективности. В течение времени рекомендации по национальным протоколам лечения в Индии менялись, и ивермектин в конечном итоге был исключен из списка рекомендованных средств. Нет доказательств, что центральное правительство заменило вакцинацию на ивермектин как основную стратегию.

Случаи заболевания COVID-19 и открытие Тадж-Махала

Пост утверждает, что случаи «сильно снизились» после этих предполагаемых изменений в политики, что позволило открыть Тадж-Махал. Хотя действительно, после смертельной второй волны случаи заболевания в Индии резко снизились к июню и июлю 2021 года, этот спад совпал с резким ростом вакцинации, продолжением обязательств по ношению масок и введением местных ограничений. Открытие Тадж-Махала и других туристических достопримечательностей было связано с уменьшением случаев заболевания и более широким ослаблением карантинных мер, а не с прекращением вакцинации или исключительным использованием ивермектина.

Заключение

Утверждение, что Индия прекратила вакцинацию населения и вместо этого зависела от ивермектина, что привело к резкому падению случаев заболевания COVID-19 и открытию Тадж-Махала, не подтверждается доказательствами. Вакцинационная кампания в Индии продолжалась на протяжении всей пандемии и сыграла ключевую роль в контроле последующих волн. Ивермектин использовался в ограниченных контекстах, но не являлся заменой вакцин на национальном уровне. Открытие туристических достопримечательностей было следствием снижения количества случаев заболевания, которые были повлияны множеством мер общественного здоровья, а не отказом от вакцинации в пользу ивермектина.

article_content:
A claim circulating on social media asserts that people who received COVID-19 vaccines will die within 10 years of vaccination. This alarming statement has sparked concern and confusion, contributing to ongoing misinformation about vaccine safety. To assess the validity of this claim, it is crucial to examine the context, available scientific evidence, and expert consensus regarding the long-term effects of COVID-19 vaccines.

The claim appears to stem from persistent misinformation campaigns that have accompanied the global rollout of COVID-19 vaccines. Since the development and deployment of vaccines in late 2020 and early 2021, a variety of unfounded assertions have emerged online, ranging from the vaccines causing infertility to altering human DNA. The notion that all vaccinated individuals will die within a decade is among the most extreme and unsupported claims circulated.

COVID-19 vaccines, including mRNA vaccines like Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, as well as viral vector vaccines such as Johnson & Johnson and AstraZeneca, underwent rigorous clinical trials before receiving emergency use authorization or full approval. These trials involved tens of thousands of participants and have been supplemented by real-world data from billions of vaccine doses administered worldwide. Throughout this process, vaccine safety profiles have been closely monitored by health agencies and independent researchers.

To date, there is no scientific evidence to support the idea that COVID-19 vaccines cause fatal long-term effects or that they will inevitably lead to death within a specific timeframe, such as 10 years. The most common side effects are mild and short-lived, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, or mild fever. Serious side effects are extremely rare and are typically identified and addressed through ongoing surveillance systems. No credible biological mechanism has been identified that would cause a vaccinated person to experience fatal consequences years after receiving the vaccine.

Experts in immunology and epidemiology emphasize that the vast majority of vaccine components are cleared from the body within days to weeks. The immune response generated is similar to what occurs after exposure to any pathogen or vaccine. Historical data from other vaccines, such as those for measles or polio, demonstrate that adverse effects are almost always seen within weeks or months, not years or decades after vaccination.

Furthermore, major health organizations, including national regulatory bodies and the World Health Organization, continue to review vaccine safety data and have not issued any warnings suggesting a shortened lifespan for vaccinated individuals. On the contrary, vaccines have played a critical role in reducing severe illness, hospitalizations, and deaths associated with COVID-19.

In summary, the claim that people who received COVID-19 vaccines will die within 10 years is not supported by any credible scientific data or expert analysis. COVID-19 vaccines remain a safe and effective tool for preventing disease and saving lives. Spreading unfounded assertions about vaccine safety undermines public health efforts and can contribute to vaccine hesitancy, putting more people at risk from preventable illness.

article_content:
A recent social media post has gone viral, claiming that “a study from India proves hydroxychloroquine is effective for COVID-19 prophylaxis.” This statement has reignited debate around the use of hydroxychloroquine, an anti-malarial drug that gained international attention early in the COVID-19 pandemic. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it’s important to examine the scientific evidence, the findings of relevant studies from India, and the current consensus among health authorities.

Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) was proposed as a potential treatment and preventive measure against COVID-19 in early 2020, based on laboratory studies showing antiviral properties. As cases surged worldwide, several countries, including India, initiated clinical trials to determine whether HCQ could prevent infection among high-risk groups, such as healthcare workers.

The social media claim references a study conducted by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), which examined the prophylactic use of HCQ among healthcare personnel. The observational study suggested that healthcare workers who took HCQ had a lower risk of contracting COVID-19 compared to those who did not. These early results led the Indian government to recommend HCQ as a preventive measure for certain frontline workers during the initial months of the pandemic.

However, it is crucial to understand the limitations of the cited study. Being observational in nature, the research did not randomly assign participants to treatment or control groups. As a result, the possibility of confounding factors—such as differences in exposure risk, adherence to other preventive measures, or reporting bias—cannot be ruled out. Observational studies can generate hypotheses but are generally considered less reliable than randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in establishing causality.

Subsequent to the ICMR study, several RCTs were conducted globally to rigorously test the effectiveness of hydroxychloroquine for both treatment and prevention of COVID-19. These studies, including some conducted in India, generally found that hydroxychloroquine did not significantly reduce the risk of infection or improve outcomes for COVID-19 patients. As more robust evidence accumulated, international health organizations, such as the World Health Organization and the US Food and Drug Administration, recommended against the routine use of hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19 prophylaxis or treatment due to lack of efficacy and potential side effects.

In summary, while an early observational study from India did suggest a potential benefit of hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19 prophylaxis, this evidence was preliminary and not definitive. Larger, better-designed trials have since failed to confirm these findings. Therefore, the claim that a study from India “proves” hydroxychloroquine is effective for COVID-19 prevention is misleading. article_content:
A recent social media post claims that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has stopped using RT-PCR tests because they are not effective at detecting COVID-19. This statement has generated confusion and concern about the accuracy of COVID-19 testing in the United States. A closer examination of the facts reveals that the claim is misleading and omits significant context about the role and effectiveness of RT-PCR testing.

Reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) tests have been the gold standard for detecting SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, since the early days of the pandemic. RT-PCR works by amplifying viral genetic material in a sample, allowing even very small amounts of virus to be detected. This high sensitivity is why RT-PCR tests are widely considered highly effective for diagnosing active COVID-19 infection.

The confusion seems to stem from a CDC announcement made in 2021 regarding the discontinuation of its own Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for the CDC 2019-Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) Real-Time RT-PCR Diagnostic Panel. This was the first COVID-19 test developed by the CDC and distributed to public health laboratories in the early stages of the pandemic. The CDC decided to withdraw its request for EUA for this specific test by the end of 2021, but this did not mean that RT-PCR testing as a whole was deemed ineffective or discontinued.

Instead, the decision reflected the rapid advancement and proliferation of COVID-19 testing technology. By mid-2021, hundreds of commercial and public health laboratories had developed and received authorization for their own RT-PCR tests and other forms of molecular diagnostics, many of which offered improved automation, higher throughput, and the ability to simultaneously detect multiple respiratory viruses, such as influenza and RSV, alongside COVID-19. The CDC encouraged laboratories to adopt these newer, multipathogen panels in anticipation of broader respiratory illness surveillance.

Importantly, the discontinuation of the CDC’s original test does not imply that RT-PCR testing is ineffective. On the contrary, RT-PCR remains the standard method for diagnosing COVID-19 due to its accuracy and sensitivity. The CDC’s move was an administrative update to phase out an early test in favor of more advanced and comprehensive diagnostics, not an indictment of the RT-PCR methodology itself.

In summary, the claim that the CDC is no longer using RT-PCR tests because they are not effective at detecting COVID-19 is inaccurate. The CDC has retired its initial RT-PCR assay, but RT-PCR technology continues to be widely employed across the United States and globally as a reliable tool for COVID-19 detection. The evolution of testing strategies reflects improvements in diagnostic technology and public health surveillance, not a fundamental problem with RT-PCR testing. It is important to distinguish between the discontinuation of a specific test and the continued use of a proven testing method.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that people who contract COVID-19 after being vaccinated have a higher viral load compared to those who are unvaccinated. This statement has sparked confusion and concern, particularly as viral load is often discussed in relation to how infectious a person might be and the potential severity of illness. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine what current scientific evidence says about COVID-19, vaccination status, and viral load.

Viral load refers to the amount of SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19) present in a person's body, typically measured using a nasal or throat swab. Higher viral loads are often associated with increased ability to spread the virus to others and potentially more severe illness. Vaccines against COVID-19 were developed to reduce the risk of severe disease, hospitalization, and death, and they have been shown to be highly effective at doing so.

The claim that vaccinated people who become infected (so-called "breakthrough infections") carry a higher viral load than unvaccinated individuals is misleading and not supported by the majority of research. Early in the pandemic, and before the emergence of certain variants such as Delta and Omicron, studies generally found that vaccinated individuals who became infected had lower viral loads than their unvaccinated counterparts. This was attributed to the immune response primed by vaccination, which helped control the virus more quickly.

With the emergence of the Delta variant, some studies observed that viral loads in breakthrough cases could be similar to those in unvaccinated individuals, particularly at the peak of infection. However, these studies did not show higher viral loads in vaccinated individuals; rather, they indicated that the initial viral loads could be comparable. Importantly, subsequent research also found that vaccinated individuals tend to clear the virus more rapidly, meaning their period of infectiousness is typically shorter than in unvaccinated people.

Furthermore, the risk of developing severe illness remains significantly lower for vaccinated individuals, even if they do become infected. Vaccination continues to provide robust protection against hospitalization and death, especially when up-to-date with booster doses. While waning immunity and the emergence of new variants can affect the overall effectiveness against infection, the core benefit of vaccination is maintained.

There is no credible evidence from peer-reviewed studies to support the claim that vaccinated people who contract COVID-19 have higher viral loads than those who are unvaccinated. The available data indicate that, at most, viral loads may be similar in the early stages of infection, but vaccinated people are likely to clear the virus faster and are better protected against severe outcomes. Claims to the contrary misrepresent the scientific consensus and may contribute to vaccine hesitancy.

In summary, the assertion that vaccination leads to higher viral loads in breakthrough COVID-19 cases is inaccurate. Vaccines remain a critical tool in controlling the pandemic, reducing both the risk of severe disease and overall transmission within the community.

Ово тврђење је изазвало мешану реакцију и тревогу, посебно зато што вирусна бару често се увазређује у односу на колико је један људ уместно заразан и потенцијалну тежину болести. Да бисмо проценили тачност овог тврђења, важно је да проучимо шта савремена научна доказивања кажу о COVID-19, стању вакцинације и вирусној бару.

Вирусна бару одређује количину SARS-CoV-2 (вируса који изазива COVID-19) у телу особе, обично мерећи се носним или грљаном узимањем узорка. Већа вирусна бару је често повезана са повећаном могућност да се вирус преноси на других особа и потенцијално већом тежином болести. Вакцине против COVID-19 су развијене да смање ризик од теже болест, болнице и смртности, и показале су високу ефикасност у овом узимању.

Тврђење да су особе које су вакцинирание и заражене (тако зване "пролазне инфекције") имале већу вирусну бару него незаражени луђи је неправилно и не подржано већином истраживања. На почетку пандемије, пре појаве одређених варијанти као што су Делта и Омикрон, истраживања су углавном показала да су особе које су вакцинирание и заражене имале нижу вирусну бару у поређењу са незараженим особама. Ово је било приписано имунолошком одговору који је промотрован вакцинацијом, што је помогло брже контроли вируса.

Са појавом варијанте Делта, нека истраживања су приметила да је вирусна бару у пролазним случајевима могла бити слична онима код незаражених особа, посебно у току врху заразе. Међутим, ова истраживања нису показала већу вирусну бару код вакцинираних особа; уместо тога, су указала да су почетне вирусне бару могле бити сличне. Важно је да је потом истраживање такође показало да вакцинирани особи често брже уклањају вирус, што значи да њихов период заразности обично није дужи него код незаражених особа.

Додатно, ризик развоја теже болести остаје значајно нижи за вакцинираних особа, чак и ако постану заражени. Вакцинација наставља да пружа одличну заштиту против болнице и смртности, посебно када су узети потенцијални дози. Иако опадајућа имунитет и појава нових варијанти могу да утицају на општу ефикасност против заражења, керна корист вакцинације је одржана.

Нема надежних доказа из истраживања која су пронађена од стране стрuчних суда да подржавају тврђење да вакцинирани особи које зараже COVID-19 имају већу вирусну бару него онима који нису вакцинирани. Доступна податка указују да, највише, вирусна бару могу бити слична у раном фази заразе, али вакцинирани особи вероватно брже уклањају вирус и имају бољу заштиту против тежих последица. Тврђења у супротном се несугласно са научним консензусом и могу да допринесу забринутости у вези са вакцинацијом.

Узимајући у обзир, тврђење да вакцинација довodi до веће вирусне бару у пролазним случајевима заразе COVID-19 је нетачно. Вакцине остају критични инструмент у контроли пандемије, смањујући и ризик од теже болест и општу пренос у средишту.

article_content:
As the COVID-19 pandemic continues to evolve, questions and claims about immunity and vaccination have become common across social media platforms. One such claim asserts that people who have previously had COVID-19 do not need to get vaccinated because they are already immune. This article will examine the validity of this statement, providing context and analysis from a scientific and public health perspective.

Understanding Immunity After Infection

When a person is infected with SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, their immune system responds by producing antibodies and activating other immune defenses. This response can provide some level of protection against reinfection, known as "natural immunity." However, the strength and duration of this immunity can vary significantly from person to person. Factors influencing this variability include the severity of the initial infection, the individual’s age, and underlying health conditions.

Early in the pandemic, it was unclear how long natural immunity might last or how effectively it could prevent future infections, especially as new variants of the virus emerged. Over time, studies have shown that natural immunity does offer some protection against reinfection, but this protection can diminish over months. Additionally, natural immunity may not be as robust against newer variants, which can partially evade immune responses generated by prior infection.

The Role of Vaccines After Infection

Vaccines against COVID-19 were developed to safely induce immunity without the risks associated with infection. Clinical data have demonstrated that vaccination significantly reduces the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death, even in people who have previously been infected.

Importantly, research has shown that individuals who receive a COVID-19 vaccine after recovering from infection—often referred to as "hybrid immunity"—develop stronger and more durable protection compared to those who rely on natural immunity alone. This enhanced immunity is particularly important in the context of emerging variants, which may partially escape the immune response generated by prior infection.

Public Health Recommendations

Major health organizations and public health authorities recommend vaccination for all eligible individuals, regardless of prior infection status. This guidance is based on accumulating evidence that vaccination provides a reliable and predictable boost to immunity, reduces the risk of reinfection, and helps prevent the spread of the virus within communities.

It is also worth noting that relying solely on natural immunity comes with significant risks. COVID-19 infection can result in severe disease, long-term complications (commonly referred to as "long COVID"), and death. Vaccination offers a safer route to immunity without exposing individuals to these risks.

Conclusion

The claim that people who had COVID-19 do not need vaccines because they are already immune does not reflect the current understanding of immunity and public health best practices. While natural infection does confer some level of immunity, vaccination is recommended to ensure stronger, broader, and longer-lasting protection against COVID-19 and its variants. Vaccination remains a critical tool in controlling the pandemic and protecting both individuals and communities.

Sementara pandemi COVID-19 terus berkembang, pertanyaan dan klaim terkait imunitas dan vaksinasi menjadi umum di berbagai platform media sosial. Salah satu klaim tersebut menyatakan bahwa orang yang pernah terinfeksi COVID-19 tidak perlu mendapatkan vaksin karena sudah memiliki imunitas. Artikel ini akan mengevaluasi validitas pernyataan tersebut, memberikan konteks dan analisis dari perspektif ilmiah dan kesehatan masyarakat.

Memahami Imunitas Setelah Infeksi

Ketika seseorang terinfeksi oleh SARS-CoV-2, virus penyebab COVID-19, sistem imun mereka bereaksi dengan memproduksi antibodi dan mengaktifkan pertahanan imun lainnya. Respons ini dapat memberikan perlindungan tertentu terhadap reinfeksi, yang dikenal sebagai "imunitas alami." Namun, tingkat kekuatan dan durasi imunitas ini dapat bervariasi secara signifikan dari satu orang ke orang lain. Faktor-faktor yang memengaruhi variasi ini mencakup tingkat keparahan infeksi awal, usia individu, serta kondisi kesehatan dasar.

Pada awal pandemi, belum jelas berapa lama imunitas alami dapat bertahan atau seberapa efektif ia dapat mencegah infeksi di masa depan, terutama seiring munculnya variant baru virus tersebut. Seiring waktu, studi menunjukkan bahwa imunitas alami memberikan perlindungan tertentu terhadap reinfeksi, tetapi perlindungan ini bisa berkurang dalam bulan-bulan. Selain itu, imunitas alami mungkin tidak sekuat terhadap variant baru, yang dapat sebagian menghindari respons imun yang dihasilkan oleh infeksi sebelumnya.

Peran Vaksin Setelah Infeksi

Vaksin melawan COVID-19 dikembangkan untuk secara aman menginduksi imunitas tanpa risiko yang terkait dengan infeksi. Data klinis telah menunjukkan bahwa vaksinasi secara signifikan mengurangi risiko penyakit berat, rawat inap, dan kematian, bahkan pada orang yang pernah terinfeksi sebelumnya.

Pentingnya, penelitian menunjukkan bahwa individu yang menerima vaksin COVID-19 setelah pulih dari infeksi—sering disebut sebagai "imunitas hibrida"—mengembangkan perlindungan yang lebih kuat dan lebih tahan lama dibandingkan mereka yang hanya bergantung pada imunitas alami. Perlindungan yang ditingkatkan ini sangat penting dalam konteks variant baru, yang mungkin sebagian menghindari respons imun yang dihasilkan oleh infeksi sebelumnya.

Rekomendasi Kesehatan Masyarakat

Organisasi kesehatan utama dan otoritas kesehatan masyarakat merekomendasikan vaksinasi bagi semua individu yang memenuhi syarat, terlepas dari status infeksi sebelumnya. Panduan ini didasarkan pada bukti yang terkumpul bahwa vaksinasi memberikan peningkatan imunitas yang dapat diandalkan dan prediktabel, mengurangi risiko reinfeksi, serta membantu mencegah penyebaran virus di dalam komunitas.

Perlu diperhatikan pula bahwa mengandalkan hanya imunitas alami memiliki risiko signifikan. Infeksi COVID-19 dapat menyebabkan penyakit berat, komplikasi jangka panjang (yang sering disebut sebagai "long COVID"), dan kematian. Vaksinasi menawarkan jalur imunitas yang lebih aman tanpa mengungkapkan individu pada risiko-risiko tersebut.

Kesimpulan

Klaim bahwa orang yang pernah terinfeksi COVID-19 tidak perlu divaksinasi karena sudah memiliki imunitas tidak mencerminkan pemahaman terkini tentang imunitas dan praktik terbaik bidang kesehatan masyarakat. Meskipun infeksi alami memberikan tingkat imunitas tertentu, vaksinasi dianjurkan untuk memastikan perlindungan yang lebih kuat, lebih luas, dan lebih tahan lama terhadap COVID-19 serta variant-variantnya. Vaksinasi tetap merupakan alat kritis dalam mengendalikan pandemi dan melindungi baik individu maupun komunitas.

article_content:
A social media post claims, “An Israeli study proves that contracting the disease gives you better immunity than being vaccinated.” This statement refers to research conducted in Israel comparing natural immunity from a previous COVID-19 infection to immunity acquired through vaccination. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it’s important to examine the context and findings of the referenced study, as well as what is currently known about COVID-19 immunity in general.

The Israeli study most often cited in this context was conducted in 2021 and involved a large population group. Its main focus was to compare the immunity of individuals who had recovered from a prior COVID-19 infection (natural immunity) to those who had received two doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine (vaccine-induced immunity). The study found that, during a period when the Delta variant was the dominant strain, people who had not been previously infected but were fully vaccinated were more likely to experience a breakthrough infection than those who had recovered from COVID-19. In other words, natural immunity appeared to provide stronger protection against reinfection compared to the two-dose vaccine regimen, at least over the time frame studied and specifically regarding the Delta variant.

However, there are important nuances and caveats that the social media post overlooks. First, the study’s results do not suggest that intentionally contracting COVID-19 is a preferable or safer way to achieve immunity. COVID-19 carries significant risks, including severe illness, long-term complications, and death, particularly for older adults and those with underlying health conditions. Vaccination, on the other hand, provides a controlled and much safer means to develop immunity without the risks associated with infection.

Second, immunity—whether from infection or vaccination—can wane over time, and new variants can alter the effectiveness of both types of immunity. The Israeli study primarily examined the Delta variant, which is no longer the dominant strain in circulation. The emergence of newer variants, such as Omicron, has shown that both natural and vaccine-induced immunity can be partially evaded, though vaccines continue to provide strong protection against severe disease and hospitalization.

Additionally, public health experts emphasize that the best protection against COVID-19 is achieved through vaccination, even for those who have previously been infected. Subsequent research has shown that so-called “hybrid immunity”—immunity acquired from both vaccination and a prior infection—offers the broadest and most durable protection against the virus.

In conclusion, while the Israeli study cited does suggest that natural immunity from a previous SARS-CoV-2 infection provided stronger protection against reinfection than vaccination alone during the Delta wave, it does not “prove” that contracting the disease is better than vaccination overall. The risks associated with infection far outweigh those of vaccination, and vaccination remains the recommended and safer path to immunity. The claim as presented lacks crucial context and oversimplifies complex scientific findings.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed that new variants of the virus responsible for COVID-19 were caused by the vaccine itself. This assertion has sparked widespread discussion and concern, prompting many to question the origins of new coronavirus variants and the role, if any, of vaccines in their emergence. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine the available evidence, the CDC’s official communications, and the scientific understanding of viral evolution.

The claim hinges on the idea that vaccination against COVID-19 is directly responsible for the development of new variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. According to virologists and public health experts, viruses mutate over time through random genetic changes that occur as they replicate. These mutations can sometimes result in new variants, some of which may spread more easily or evade parts of the immune response. The primary driver of new COVID-19 variants has been widespread transmission of the virus, not vaccination.

The CDC has repeatedly stated that the rise of new variants is a natural part of viral evolution, particularly when the virus is allowed to circulate widely in populations. As more people become infected, the virus has more opportunities to mutate. The agency has consistently encouraged vaccination as a means to reduce the spread of the virus, which in turn decreases the chances for new variants to emerge.

There is no official statement, report, or confirmation from the CDC suggesting that COVID-19 vaccines are responsible for creating new variants. In fact, the CDC has explained that vaccines help to reduce the overall burden of infection, thereby limiting the virus’s ability to mutate and form new variants. While breakthrough infections can occur—meaning vaccinated individuals can sometimes become infected—current evidence shows that these cases are less frequent and less severe compared to infections in unvaccinated individuals.

Some social media users have misinterpreted scientific discussions about “immune escape,” a process where a virus evolves to partially evade immune protection, as evidence that vaccines cause variants. However, immune escape can occur in any context where the virus is under selective pressure, including natural immunity from prior infection. Importantly, the vast majority of variants to date have emerged in populations with low vaccination coverage, not as a direct result of vaccination.

In summary, the claim that the CDC has confirmed vaccines as the cause of new COVID-19 variants is not supported by scientific evidence or official statements from the agency. The best available data indicate that uncontrolled viral spread is the most significant factor in the emergence of new variants. Vaccination remains a key tool in reducing infections and, by extension, the likelihood of new variants developing. It is crucial to rely on verified information from credible sources when assessing claims about public health and vaccines.

In recent days, a social media post has been circulating that claims Anvisa, Brazil’s National Health Surveillance Agency, has admitted that masks are not effective against COVID-19. This assertion has raised considerable debate, especially as mask-wearing continues to be a public health topic around the world. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to review official statements from Anvisa, the scientific consensus on mask efficacy, and the broader context of mask recommendations during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Anvisa is a regulatory agency responsible for protecting and promoting public health in Brazil, including oversight of medications, medical devices, and public health measures. Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, Anvisa has played a central role in guiding policies to mitigate the spread of the virus, including recommendations on the use of masks. Throughout 2020 and 2021, Anvisa issued guidelines supporting the use of masks in crowded and enclosed public spaces. These recommendations were based on evolving evidence from global health authorities and research on respiratory virus transmission.

The social media post claims that Anvisa “admitted” that masks are not effective. This suggests a reversal in official guidance or an acknowledgment that masks do not work to prevent COVID-19. However, a review of Anvisa’s official communications does not support this claim. While Anvisa, like many public agencies, has updated its mask guidance over time—reflecting new data, vaccine rollouts, and changing epidemiological circumstances—it has never issued a blanket statement declaring masks ineffective against COVID-19. Instead, the agency has consistently emphasized that mask efficacy depends on several factors, including the mask type, correct usage, and the context in which it is worn.

For example, cloth masks were recommended early in the pandemic when surgical and N95 masks were in short supply. As evidence mounted that medical-grade masks provided greater protection, recommendations shifted accordingly. Anvisa has also acknowledged that masks alone are not a “silver bullet” and must be combined with other measures such as vaccination, hand hygiene, and social distancing. This nuanced approach is consistent with the broader scientific understanding: masks can reduce the transmission of respiratory droplets and are most effective when used properly and alongside other preventive strategies.

The claim that Anvisa admitted masks are not effective misrepresents the agency’s position. There is no public record of Anvisa making such a blanket statement. The agency’s communications stress that mask effectiveness varies but does not deny their role in reducing transmission, especially in high-risk environments. It is possible that the claim originated from a misinterpretation of statements regarding changes in mask guidance—such as recommendations for mask usage decreasing in certain settings as vaccination rates increased and case numbers fell.

In summary, the social media post’s claim is inaccurate. Anvisa has not admitted that masks are ineffective against COVID-19. Instead, the agency has provided evolving guidance based on scientific evidence, consistently supporting mask use as part of a comprehensive approach to controlling the virus. Misrepresenting official statements can undermine public health efforts and sow confusion during a pandemic when clear communication is crucial.

Anvisa, ਬ੍ਰਾਜ਼ੀਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਹਤ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਸਹਿਯੋਗ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੀ ਨਿਯਮਨ ਏਜੰਸੀ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਔਸ਼ਧੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਚੀਜ਼ਾਂ, ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਉਪਕਰਣ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਹਤ ਮਾਪਦੰਡਾਂ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਰਾਨੀ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਕੋਰੋਨਾਵਾਇਰਸ ਮਹਾਮਾਰੀ ਦੇ ਆਰੰਭ ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ, Anvisa ਨੇ ਵਾਇਰਸ ਦੇ ਫੈਲਣ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਲਈ ਨੀਤੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਖ ਸੂਚਨਾ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੀ ਸੁਝਾਵ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹੈ। 2020 ਅਤੇ 2021 ਦੌਰਾਨ, Anvisa ਨੇ ਭੀੜ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਬੰਦ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਜਗ੍ਹਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੀ ਸੁਝਾਵ ਦੇ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕੀਤੇ। ਇਹ ਸੁਝਾਵ ਦੁਨੀਆ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਹਤ ਅਧਿਕਾਰੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਅਧਾਰ ਤੇ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਸ਼ੋਧਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਣਿਕ ਸਬੂਤ ਅਤੇ ਹਾਲਤ ਦੇ ਰੋਗ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵਾ ਦੇ ਅਧਾਰ ਤੇ ਬਣਾਏ ਗਏ ਸਨ।

ਸਮਾਜਿਕ ਮੀਡੀਆ ਪੋਸਟ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ Anvisa ਨੇ "ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਕੀਤੀ" ਹੈ ਕਿ ਮਾਸਕ ਕੋਰੋਨਾਵਾਇਰਸ ਵਿਰੁੱਧ ਅਸਰਦਾਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੀ ਮੰਨਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਆਫ਼ਸ਼ਲ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਰੁੱਧ ਜਾਂ ਕੋਰੋਨਾਵਾਇਰਸ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਸਕ ਕੈਸ਼ੀਅਰ ਨਾ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਮਾਨਤਾ ਹੈ। ਪਰ, Anvisa ਦੇ ਆਫ਼ਸ਼ਲ ਸੰਚਾਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਇਸ ਦਾਅਵੇ ਦਾ ਸਮਰਥਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦੀ। ਹਾਲਾਂਕਿ, Anvisa, ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਏਜੰਸੀਆਂ ਜਿਵੇਂ ਹੀ, ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਅਪਡੇਟ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਨਵੀਆਂ ਸੰਗਠਨ, ਟੀਕਾਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਸੰਚਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਬਦਲੇ ਰੋਗ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਸਥਿਤੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਅਧਾਰ ਤੇ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਇਸ ਨੇ ਕੋਰੋਨਾਵਾਇਰਸ ਵਿਰੁੱਧ ਮਾਸਕ ਅਸਰਦਾਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ ਦੀ ਕੋਈ ਸਾਰਾ ਘੋਸ਼ਣਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਨੇ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਅਸਰਦਾਰਤਾ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਦਿਆਂ ਕਿ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਅਸਰਦਾਰਤਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਕਾਰਨ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਕਿਸਮ, ਸਹੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ, ਅਤੇ ਇਸਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਉੱਪਰ ਨਿਰਭਰ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਨੂੰ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ।

ਉਦਾਹਰਨ ਲਈ, ਮਹਾਮਾਰੀ ਦੇ ਆਰੰਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੱਪੜੇ ਵਾਲੇ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਸੁਝਾਵ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਸੀ, ਜਦੋਂ ਸਰਜਨੀ ਅਤੇ N95 ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਕਮੀ ਸੀ। ਜਦੋਂ ਸਬੂਤ ਮੁਕਾਬਲਤ: ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਗ੍ਰੇਡ ਮਾਸਕ ਵੱਧ ਰੋਕਥਾਮ ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਣ ਦੀ ਸੰਖਿਆ ਵਧਦੀ ਗਈ, ਤਾਂ ਸੁਝਾਵ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਬਦਲੇ। Anvisa ਨੇ ਇਹ ਵੀ ਮਾਨਤਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਮਾਸਕ ਅਜੇ ਇੱਕ "ਸਿਲਵਰ ਬਾਲਟ" ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਟੀਕਾਕਰਨ, ਹੱਥ ਸਾਫ਼ਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਮਾਜਿਕ ਦੂਰੀ ਜੋੜਨਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਚੁੰਮੇ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵੇ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਖ ਵਿਗਿਆਨਿਕ ਸਮਝ ਨਾਲ ਸਬੰਧ ਹੈ: ਮਾਸਕ ਹਾਲਤ ਦੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਦੇ ਵਿਸ਼ਾ ਨੂੰ ਘਟਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਇਸਦੀ ਅਸਰਦਾਰਤਾ ਸਹੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਰੋਕਥਾਮ ਦੀਆਂ ਸਟਰਾਟੇਜੀਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਸਹੀ ਹੈ।

Anvisa ਨੇ ਮਾਸਕ ਅਸਰਦਾਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਕਲਾਈਮ ਗਲਤ ਹੈ। ਆਫ਼ਸ਼ਲ ਰਿਕਾਰਡ ਵਿੱਚ Anvisa ਨੇ ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਇੱਕ ਸਾਰਾ ਘੋਸ਼ਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤੀ। ਏਜੰਸੀ ਦੇ ਸੰਚਾਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਅਸਰਦਾਰਤਾ ਬਦਲੇ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਕੁੱਝ ਰੋਕਥਾਮ ਦੀ ਭੂਮਿਕਾ ਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਕੁੱਝ ਨਾ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਖਾਸ ਕਰਕੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਸਥਿਤੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਰੋਗ ਦੀ ਸੰਖਿਆ ਘੱਟ ਗਈ। ਸੰਭਵ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ, ਇਹ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਮਾਸਕ ਸੁਝਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਬਦਲੇ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਵਲੀ ਦੀ ਗਲਤ ਵਿਵਿਧਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਉਠਿਆ ਹੈ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਟੀਕਾਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਦਰ ਵਧਦੀ ਅਤੇ ਰੋਗ ਦੀ ਸੰਖਿਆ ਘੱਟ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ, ਤਾਂ ਕੁਝ ਸਥਿਤੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਸਕ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੀ ਸੁਝਾਵ ਘੱਟ ਹੋ ਗਈ।

ਸੰਕਲਪ ਵਿੱਚ, ਸਮਾਜਿਕ ਮੀਡੀਆ ਪੋਸਟ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਗਲਤ ਹੈ। Anvisa ਨੇ ਕੋਰੋਨਾਵਾਇਰਸ ਵਿਰੁੱਧ ਮਾਸਕ ਅਸਰਦਾਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ। ਬਜਾਏ ਇਸਦੇ, ਏਜੰਸੀ ਨੇ ਵਿਗਿਆਨਿਕ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਣ ਦੇ ਆਧਾਰ ਤੇ ਅਸਰਦਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਬਦਲੇ ਸੁਝਾਵ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕੀਤੇ ਹਨ, ਜੋ ਵਾਇਰਸ ਦੀ ਨਿਯੰਤ੍ਰਣ ਲਈ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵੇ ਦਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਹੈ। ਆਫ਼ਸ਼ਲ ਘੋਸ਼ਣਾ ਨੂੰ ਗਲਤੀ ਕਰਕੇ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਕਰਨਾ ਸਿਹਤ ਕਾਰਜਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਪਹੁੰਚਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਮਾਰੀ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਸੰਚਾਰ ਦੀ ਸਪਸ਼ਟਤਾ ਲਈ ਅਸਥਿਰਤਾ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
article_summary: Um post nas redes sociais afirma que a Anvisa admitiu que máscaras não são eficazes contra o coronavírus, gerando debate. A agência brasileira, responsável por orientações de saúde, nunca emitiu declaração genérica negando a eficácia das máscaras, mas atualizou recomendações com base em evidências científicas. A afirmação é considerada uma representação imprecisa, já que a Anvisa sempre enfatizou a importância das máscaras como parte de medidas combinadas para conter a pandemia.

article_content:
A claim circulating on social media asserts that Oxford University stated 250,000 lives could be saved in Brazil if ivermectin was widely used. This assertion has gained traction in some online communities, particularly among supporters of alternative COVID-19 treatments. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to examine both the context surrounding ivermectin’s use and the official positions of Oxford University and the broader scientific community.

Ivermectin is an antiparasitic medication that has been used for decades to treat various parasitic infections in humans and animals. During the COVID-19 pandemic, interest in repurposing existing drugs led to research into ivermectin’s potential antiviral effects. Early laboratory studies suggested the drug might inhibit the replication of the SARS-CoV-2 virus under certain conditions. However, these studies utilized much higher concentrations than what is safe or achievable in humans.

As the pandemic unfolded, several clinical trials were initiated to test ivermectin’s efficacy against COVID-19. The results of these studies have been mixed and, in many cases, inconclusive. Several large, well-conducted randomized controlled trials indicated that ivermectin did not significantly reduce mortality, hospitalization, or duration of illness in COVID-19 patients compared to standard care or placebo. Regulatory agencies and health authorities, including the World Health Organization and national agencies in the United States, Europe, and Brazil, have not recommended ivermectin for the prevention or treatment of COVID-19 outside of clinical trials.

Oxford University has indeed conducted research on ivermectin through the PRINCIPLE trial, a large UK-based study evaluating potential COVID-19 treatments in community settings. The trial investigated whether ivermectin could accelerate recovery or prevent hospitalizations but did not find compelling evidence to support its use. At no point has Oxford University made an official statement claiming that widespread use of ivermectin could save 250,000 lives in Brazil or in any other country. No such figure appears in published Oxford University reports, press releases, or academic articles.

The origin of the 250,000 figure appears to be a misrepresentation or misinterpretation of scientific discussions that have occurred in public forums, often cited without direct attribution or evidence. Some proponents of ivermectin have extrapolated potential benefits based on small studies or hypothetical models, but these do not reflect the consensus of the scientific community or the official position of Oxford University.

In Brazil, the debate over ivermectin has been particularly heated, with some public figures and officials promoting the drug despite the lack of strong evidence. The Brazilian health ministry and scientific societies have ultimately advised against its use for COVID-19, aligning with international guidelines.

In summary, the claim that Oxford University stated 250,000 lives could be saved in Brazil with widespread ivermectin use is not supported by evidence. Oxford University has not made any such statement, and current research does not substantiate the claim that ivermectin is an effective lifesaving treatment for COVID-19. The promotion of this claim misrepresents the scientific consensus and may contribute to the spread of misinformation about COVID-19 treatments.

Naglalabas sa social media ang isang pahayag na nangangahulugan na ang Oxford University ay nagsasabi na maaaring i-save ang 250,000 buhay sa Brazil kung ang ivermectin ay gamitin nang malawak. Ang pahayag na ito ay nagkaroon ng malawak na suporta sa ilang mga komunidad sa online, lalo na sa mga tagasuporta ng mga alternatibong gamot para sa COVID-19. Upang masuri ang kahusayan ng pahayag na ito, kinakailangan ang pag-unawa sa konteksto ng paggamit ng ivermectin at ang mga opinyon ng Oxford University at ng mas malawak na komunidad ng mga siyentipiko.

Ang ivermectin ay isang gamot na antiparasito na ginagamit para sa mga dekada upang tratuhin ang iba't ibang mga parasitiko na sakit sa tao at hayop. Sa panahon ng pandemya ng COVID-19, ang interes sa paggamit ng mga nangungunang gamot ay nagresulta sa mga pagsusuri sa posibleng antiviral na epekto ng ivermectin. Ang mga unang pagsusuri sa laboratorio ay nagmungkahi na ang gamot ay maaaring mamalaw sa paglalatag ng SARS-CoV-2 virus sa ilang mga kondisyon. Ngunit ang mga pagsusuri na ito ay ginagamit ang masyung mabigat na dosis kaysa sa nangangailangan o maaaring makamit sa mga tao.

Sa pagdaan ng pandemya, nagsimulang magsagawa ng mga klinikal na pagsusuri upang tukuyin ang epektibong gamit ng ivermectin laban sa COVID-19. Ang mga resulta ng mga pagsusuri ay nangunguna at hindi malinaw. Maraming malalaking, maayos na mga randomize na kontroladong pagsusuri ay nagmungkahi na ang ivermectin ay hindi nangangahulugan ng makabuluhang pagbawas sa kamatayan, pagpapadala sa ospital, o pagkakaroon ng sakit sa mga pasyente ng COVID-19 kumpara sa standard na pangangalaga o placebo. Ang mga ahensya ng regulasyon at mga awtoridad sa kalusugan, kabilang ang World Health Organization at mga nasasakop na ahensya sa Estados Unidos, Europa, at Brazil, ay hindi narekomenda ang gamit ng ivermectin para sa pag-iwas o paggamot sa COVID-19 sa labas ng mga klinikal na pagsusuri.

Nangangahulugan nga ang Oxford University ay nagsagawa ng mga pagsusuri sa ivermectin sa pamamagitan ng PRINCIPLE trial, isang malalaking UK-based na pagsusuri na nag-aaral ng mga posibleng mga gamot para sa paggamot sa komunidad na setting ng COVID-19. Ang pagsusuri ay nagsasagawa kung ang ivermectin ay maaaring mag-advance ng pagkakatugon o mapanatili ang pagpapadala sa ospital, ngunit wala itong magawa na komportable na ebidensya upang suportahan ang paggamit nito. Sa walang oras, walang nangangahulugan ang Oxford University na nagsasabi ng isang opisyales na pahayag na ang malawak na gamit ng ivermectin ay maaaring i-save ang 250,000 buhay sa Brazil o anumang iba pang bansa. Ang 250,000 figure ay walang nangangahulugan sa mga publikasyon ng Oxford University, mga pahayag sa media, o mga akademikong artikulo.

Ang pinagmulan ng 250,000 figure ay nangangahulugan na isang maliwanag na pagpapakita o maliwanag na interpretasyon ng mga pagsusuri sa publiko, na madalas na sinasalita nang walang direktang paglalarawan o ebidensya. Ang ilang mga tagasuporta ng ivermectin ay nagsusumite ng mga potensyal na benepisyo batay sa mga maliit na pagsusuri o mga hipotetikal na modelo, ngunit ang mga ito ay hindi nangangahulugan ng konsensus ng komunidad ng mga siyentipiko o ang opinyon ng Oxford University.

Sa Brazil, ang debate tungkol sa ivermectin ay naging masusing debate, may ilang mga publiko na mga tao at mga opisyales na nagpapalabas ng gamot kahit walang malakas na ebidensya. Ang mga awtoridad sa kalusugan ng Brazil at mga samahan ng siyensya ay nangangahulugan na ang gamit ng ivermectin para sa COVID-19 ay hindi dapat, na sumunod sa mga pandaigdigang mga rekomendasyon.

Sa kabuuan, ang pahayag na ang Oxford University ay nagsasabi na maaaring i-save ang 250,000 buhay sa Brazil sa pamamagitan ng malawak na gamit ng ivermectin ay hindi nangangahulugan ng ebidensya. Ang Oxford University ay walang nangangahulugan na opisyales na pahayag, at ang kasalukuyang mga pagsusuri ay hindi nangangahulugan ng pahayag na ang ivermectin ay isang epektibong gamot para i-save ang buhay sa mga pasyente ng COVID-19. In recent years, a narrative has circulated on social media claiming that the presidents of Tanzania, Haiti, and Burundi were killed because they opposed vaccines. This claim has gained traction among groups skeptical of global vaccination efforts, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. However, a detailed examination of the circumstances surrounding the deaths of these leaders and their positions on vaccines reveals a more complex reality, and the claim that they were assassinated for their vaccine stances is not supported by available evidence.

**Background and Context**

During the COVID-19 pandemic, some leaders in Africa and the Caribbean expressed skepticism toward vaccines and the pandemic’s severity. Among them were John Magufuli of Tanzania, Pierre Nkurunziza of Burundi, and Jovenel Moïse of Haiti. Their approaches to COVID-19 and vaccines drew international attention and, in some circles, suspicion following their untimely deaths.

**John Magufuli, President of Tanzania**

President John Magufuli was a vocal skeptic of COVID-19 and dismissed the efficacy of masks, testing, and vaccines. He promoted prayer and traditional remedies, and under his leadership, Tanzania stopped reporting COVID-19 data to the World Health Organization for a significant period. Magufuli died in March 2021 at the age of 61. The official cause of death was heart failure, a condition he had reportedly suffered from for a decade. However, his prolonged absence from public view prior to his death fueled rumors that he may have died of COVID-19. There has been no credible evidence presented to suggest Magufuli was assassinated or that his death was directly linked to his opposition to vaccines.

**Pierre Nkurunziza, President of Burundi**

Pierre Nkurunziza, President of Burundi from 2005 until his death in June 2020, also took a controversial stance on COVID-19. His government expelled World Health Organization officials and downplayed the threat of the virus, with skepticism regarding the need for vaccines. Nkurunziza died at age 55, with the official cause given as a heart attack. Speculation arose that he may have died from COVID-19, as his wife was reportedly hospitalized with the virus in Kenya shortly before his death. Again, there is no substantiated evidence indicating foul play, and no connection has been established between his death and his vaccine policies.

**Jovenel Moïse, President of Haiti**

Jovenel Moïse, President of Haiti, was assassinated in his home in July 2021. While Haiti had not yet begun a vaccination campaign at the time, the delay was attributed to logistical challenges and vaccine hesitancy in the population, as well as skepticism from the government. However, Moïse’s assassination was the result of a complex political plot involving mercenaries and dissent within Haiti, according to multiple investigations. There is no evidence to suggest that his death was linked to his approach to COVID-19 vaccination.

**Conclusion**

While it is true that the presidents of Tanzania, Burundi, and Haiti each exhibited skepticism toward COVID-19 vaccines or pandemic measures, the claim that they were killed for opposing vaccines is not supported by credible evidence. Magufuli and Nkurunziza died of reported natural causes, with rumors but no proof of foul play. Moïse was assassinated, but the motives were political and unrelated to vaccination policy. The narrative that these leaders were killed specifically for opposing vaccines is therefore misleading.

**จอห์น มักวูฟูลี ประธานาธิบดีของแทนซาเนีย**

ประธานาธิบดีจอห์น มักวูฟูลีเป็นผู้แสดงความไม่เชื่อมั่นอย่างชัดเจนต่อโควิด-19 และปฏิเสธประสิทธิภาพของหน้ากาก ตรวจหาเชื้อ และวัคซีน เขายังสนับสนุนการอธิษฐานและวิธีการรักษาแบบดั้งเดิม โดยภายใต้การนำของเขา แทนซาเนียได้หยุดรายงานข้อมูลโควิด-19 ต่อองค์การอนามัยโลกเป็นเวลานาน มักวูฟูลีเสียชีวิตในเดือนมีนาคม 2021 ที่อายุ 61 ปี สาเหตุทางการแพทย์ที่เป็นทางการคือภาวะหัวใจวาย ซึ่งเขาเคยเป็นมาตั้งแต่ทศวรรษที่ผ่านมา อย่างไรก็ตาม การขาดอยู่ในสายตาสาธารณะของเขาในช่วงเวลาที่ผ่านมา ก่อให้เกิดข่าวลือว่าเขาอาจเสียชีวิตจากโควิด-19 โดยไม่มีหลักฐานที่น่าเชื่อถือใด ๆ ที่ชี้ว่ามักวูฟูลีถูกสังหาร หรือว่าการเสียชีวิตของเขาเกี่ยวข้องโดยตรงกับท่าทีต่อต้านวัคซีนของเขา

**พิเอร์ เนคูรูนซิซา ประธานาธิบดีของบุรundi**

พิเอร์ เนคูรูนซิซา ประธานาธิบดีของบุรundi ตั้งแต่ปี 2005 จนถึงการเสียชีวิตของเขาในเดือนมิถุนายน 2020 ก็มีท่าทีที่ขัดแย้งต่อโควิด-19 รัฐบาลของเขาได้ขับไล่เจ้าหน้าที่ขององค์การอนามัยโลก และลดความสำคัญของภัยคุกคามจากเชื้อไวรัส โดยมีความไม่เชื่อมั่นในความจำเป็นของวัคซีน เนคูรูนซิซาเสียชีวิตในวัย 55 ปี โดยสาเหตุทางการแพทย์ที่เป็นทางการคือภาวะหัวใจวาย ความคาดเดาที่เกิดขึ้นคือเขาอาจเสียชีวิตจากโควิด-19 เนื่องจากภรรยาของเขาถูกนำตัวไปรับการรักษาในโรงพยาบาลในเคนยาไม่นานก่อนเสียชีวิต อย่างไรก็ตาม ไม่มีหลักฐานที่น่าเชื่อถือใด ๆ ที่ชี้ว่ามีการกระทำผิดกฎหมาย และไม่มีการเชื่อมโยงระหว่างการเสียชีวิตของเขาและนโยบายวัคซีนของเขานะ

**โจเวนเอล มัวส์ ประธานาธิบดีของฮัดส์**

โจเวนเอล มัวส์ ประธานาธิบดีของฮัดส์ ถูกสังหารในบ้านของเขาในเดือนกรกฎาคม 2021 แม้ว่าฮัดส์จะยังไม่ได้เริ่มโครงการฉีดวัคซีนในขณะนั้น แต่การล่าช้าถูกอธิบายว่าเกิดจากความท้าทายด้านการจัดส่ง และความลังเลในการฉีดวัคซีนของประชากร รวมถึงความไม่เชื่อมั่นของรัฐบาล อย่างไรก็ตาม การสังหารมัวส์เป็นผลจากการสมคบคิดทางการเมืองที่ซับซ้อน ซึ่งมีผู้ตั้งร้ายและแรงงานข้ามชาติเข้ามามีส่วนร่วมตามการสอบสวนหลายกรณี ไม่มีหลักฐานใด ๆ ที่ชี้ว่าการเสียชีวิตของเขาเกี่ยวข้องกับแนวทางของเขาต่อการฉีดวัคซีนต่อโควิด-19

**สรุป**

แม้ว่าประธานาธิบดีของแทนซาเนีย บุรundi และฮัดส์จะมีท่าทีที่ไม่เชื่อมั่นต่อวัคซีนโควิด-19 หรือมาตรการต่อต้านการระบาดของโรค แต่ข้อกล่าวหาที่ว่าพวกเขาถูกสังหารเพราะต่อต้านวัคซีนไม่มีหลักฐานที่น่าเชื่อถือ แมกวูฟูลีและเนคูรูนซิซาเสียชีวิตจากสาเหตุตามธรรมชาติที่รายงานไว้ มีข่าวลือแต่ไม่มีหลักฐานว่ามีการกระทำผิดกฎหมาย ส่วนมัวส์ถูกสังหาร แต่จุดประสงค์คือการเมืองและไม่เกี่ยวข้องกับนโยบายวัคซีน ดังนั้น ข้อความที่ว่าผู้นำเหล่านี้ถูกสังหารเฉพาะเพราะต่อต้านวัคซีนจึงเป็นข่าวที่ผิดพลาด

In recent years, concerns about vaccine ingredients have proliferated across social media, leading to widespread speculation and misinformation. One claim frequently encountered is that vaccines contain graphene oxide, a compound sometimes discussed in the context of nanotechnology and medical research. This article examines the validity of this claim and provides context for understanding vaccine composition and the role of graphene oxide in medical science.

Graphene oxide is a derivative of graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice. Due to its unique properties—such as high conductivity and strength—graphene oxide has attracted attention for potential applications in electronics, energy storage, and even biomedical research, including drug delivery and biosensing. However, its use in commercial and clinical applications remains largely experimental.

Vaccines, whether used to prevent diseases such as influenza, measles, or COVID-19, contain specific components designed to trigger an immune response. The main ingredients typically include antigens (the active component), adjuvants (to enhance the immune response), stabilizers, and preservatives. In recent years, mRNA vaccines—such as those used for COVID-19—have used lipid nanoparticles to deliver genetic instructions to cells. These lipid nanoparticles do not contain graphene oxide; they are composed of specific fats, cholesterol, and other molecules designed to safely transport mRNA.

The claim that vaccines contain graphene oxide appears to have stemmed from confusion or deliberate misinformation. Some social media posts and videos have circulated purportedly showing laboratory analyses indicating the presence of graphene oxide in vaccine samples. These reports, however, lack credible scientific backing and have not been corroborated by independent or regulatory laboratories. Health authorities and vaccine manufacturers have repeatedly stated that graphene oxide is not an ingredient in any approved vaccine.

Regulatory agencies, such as the Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency, require comprehensive disclosure and review of all vaccine ingredients before approval. Ingredient lists for vaccines are publicly available and do not include graphene oxide. Any deviation from these lists—particularly the introduction of a novel compound like graphene oxide—would require significant regulatory scrutiny and public disclosure.

Concerns about vaccine safety are valid and should be addressed through transparent scientific investigation. However, the spread of misinformation can undermine public trust in vaccination programs and hinder efforts to control infectious diseases. While graphene oxide may play a role in future medical technologies, there is currently no evidence to support the claim that it is present in vaccines administered to the public.

In summary, a review of vaccine ingredients, regulatory documents, and scientific literature does not support the assertion that vaccines contain graphene oxide. This claim remains unfounded and is not backed by scientific or regulatory evidence. Individuals seeking information about vaccine safety and composition are encouraged to consult reputable sources and speak with healthcare professionals.

ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડ એ ગ્રાફનનો એક સ્વરૂપ છે, જે એક છાતીની છાપના જાળના સંગઠિત કાર્બન અણુઓની એક સ્તર છે. તેના વિશિષ્ટ ગુણો - જેમ કે ઉચ્ચ ચાલકતા અને શક્તિ - તેને ઇલેક્ટ્રોનિક્સ, ઊર્જા સંગ્રહણ અને અને ચિકિત્સા શોધ, જેમ કે દવાઓનું પ્રસારણ અને જીવશોધન માટેની સાંભળી લેવામાં આવે છે. તેની કાર્યાત્મકતા કોમર્શિયલ અને ચિકિત્સાસંબંધી પ્રયોગોમાં સામાન્ય રીતે પ્રયોગાત્મક રહે છે.

દુર્બળતાઓ જેવી કે ઇન્ફ્લુએન્ઝા, મેસ્સલ્સ અથવા કોરોનાવાયરસ પ્રતિરોધ માટે વાપરવામાં આવે છે, વેક્સિન ખાસ ઘટકોનો ઉપયોગ કરે છે જે વિરોધાભાસ ઉત્પન્ન કરે છે. મુખ્ય ઘટકો સામાન્ય રીતે એન્ટિજન (સક્રિય ઘટક), એડ્જ્યુવન્ટ્સ (સંઘર્ષ ઉત્પન્ન કરવા માટે), સ્થિરકરણો અને રાખાંતરો છે. કેટલાક વર્ષો સુધી, મેસેજ આર્ના વેક્સિનો - જે કોરોનાવાયરસ માટે વાપરવામાં આવે છે - કોષોમાં આધુનિક નિર્દેશો પહોંચાડવા માટે લિપિડ નેનોપાર્ટિકલ્સનો ઉપયોગ કરે છે. આ લિપિડ નેનોપાર્ટિકલ્સમાં ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડ નથી, તેઓ ખાસ તેલ, કોલેસ્ટેરોલ અને અન્ય અણુઓના મિશ્રણ છે જે મેસેજ આર્નાને સુરક્ષિત રીતે પહોંચાડે છે.

વેક્સિનમાં ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડ હોય છે એવા દાવા તારસ્થિતિ કે અસાધારણ માહિતીના માટે ઉત્પન્ન થયો છે. કેટલાક સામાજિક મીડિયા પોસ્ટ્સ અને વીડિયોસ સામાન્ય રીતે લેબોરેટરી વિશ્લેષણ પ્રદર્શિત કરે છે જે વેક્સિન નમૂનામાં ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડની હાજરી દર્શાવે છે. તેના પરિણામો તેમની વિશ્વસનીય વૈજ્ઞાનિક પુરાવાની અભાવ છે અને સ્વતંત્ર અથવા નિયમન લેબોરેટરીઓ દ્વારા સમર્થિત નથી. આરોગ્ય અધિકારીઓ અને વેક્સિન નિર્માતાઓ સામાન્ય રીતે જણાવે છે કે ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડ કોઈપણ અપાવવામાં આવેલા વેક્સિનના ઘટકોમાં નથી.

નિયમન એજન્સીઓ, જેમ કે ફૂડ અને ડ્રગ એડમિનિસ્ટ્રેશન અને યુરોપિયન મેડિકલ એજન્સી, કોઈપણ વેક્સિનના ઘટકોની પૂર્ણ ખુલ્લી વિગતો અને મૂલ્યાંકનની માંગ કરે છે પહેલાં પ્રમાણિત કરવામાં આવે છે. વેક્સિનના ઘટકોની યાદીઓ જાહેર છે અને ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડનો સમાવેશ નથી. આ યાદીઓથી વિચલિત થવાની પ્રવૃત્તિ, વિશેષ રૂપે એક નવી સંયોજન જેવો ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડ હોય તેની પ્રવૃત્તિ માટે મોટી નિયમન તપાસ અને જાહેર કરાવાની આવશ્યકતા હોય છે.

વેક્સિનની સુરક્ષા વિશેની ચિંતાઓ સાચી છે અને તેને સ્પષ્ટ વૈજ્ઞાનિક તપાસના માધ્યમે સંબોધિત કરવી જોઈએ. તેમની પ્રસારણ સાથે અસાધારણ માહિતીની વિસ્તાર વેક્સિન પ્રોગ્રામ માટે જનતાની ભરોસાની નાશ કરી શકે છે અને સંક્રમણ રોગોને નિયંત્રિત કરવાના પ્રયત્નોને અવરોધી શકે છે. છતાં ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડ ભવિષ્યના ચિકિત્સા તકનીકોમાં ભૂમિકા ભજવી શકે છે, પરંતુ હાલમાં કોઈપણ પુરાવો છે કે તે સામાન્ય લોકોને આપવામાં આવેલા વેક્સિનમાં હોય છે.

સારાંશ, વેક્સિન ઘટકોની તપાસ, નિયમન દસ્તાવેજો અને વૈજ્ઞાનિક સાહિત્યની સમીક્ષા વેક્સિનમાં ગ્રાફન ઑક્સાઇડ હોય છે એવા દાવાને સમર્થન આપતો નથી. આ દાવો અસ્થાયી છે અને વૈજ્ઞાનિક અથવા નિયમન પુરાવા વિના છે. વેક્સિન સુરક્ષા અને ઘટકો વિશે માહિતી મેળવવા માંગતા લોકોને વિશ્વસનીય સ્ત્રોતો પર જઈ શોધવા અને ચિકિત્સકો સાથે વાત કરવા માટે આહવા છે.

A video circulating widely on social media claims to show water droplets being expelled from a syringe, with the caption alleging that the vaccine inside is being manipulated or “floated” using 5G technology. The post suggests that 5G networks are somehow interacting with the vaccine’s contents, causing the observed behavior of the liquid in the syringe.

**Background and Context**

Since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, misinformation about vaccines has proliferated online. Among the most persistent conspiracy theories are those involving 5G mobile networks. Some claims have falsely suggested that 5G technology can interact with COVID-19 vaccines, either by activating “microchips” allegedly contained within the vaccines or by manipulating their physical properties. These assertions have been widely debunked by health experts and scientists, but they continue to gain traction in certain online communities.

**Analysis of the Video Content**

The video in question shows a close-up of a syringe as water droplets are expelled from its tip. There is no visible involvement of any external device or technology, other than the hand operating the syringe. The caption, however, asserts that 5G technology is responsible for the behavior of the liquid, implying that electromagnetic waves from 5G towers or devices are causing the vaccine (or water, in this case) to “float” or behave abnormally.

To analyze this claim, it is important to understand how both syringes and 5G technology work:

- **Syringes:** When pressure is applied to the plunger of a syringe, it forces the liquid inside to exit through the needle or nozzle. The formation of droplets at the tip is a normal physical phenomenon caused by surface tension and the properties of the liquid. This occurs regardless of the type of liquid or the presence of electromagnetic fields.
  
- **5G Technology:** 5G is the fifth generation of mobile network technology. It operates by transmitting radiofrequency (RF) signals, similar to previous generations (4G, 3G). These signals are non-ionizing and cannot manipulate matter at the microscopic or macroscopic level in the manner suggested by the video. There is no known scientific mechanism by which 5G signals could cause a liquid in a syringe to “float” or behave differently.

**Scientific Consensus**

Leading scientific and health authorities have repeatedly stated that 5G radio waves are not capable of interacting with the contents of vaccines. There is no evidence that 5G signals can change the physical properties of vaccine ingredients or influence their behavior in any way. Videos showing droplets exiting a syringe are easily explained by basic physics and do not require the invocation of wireless technology.

**Conclusion**

The claim that 5G technology is causing vaccine liquid to “float” or be manipulated inside a syringe is unfounded and not supported by any scientific evidence. The video simply shows a normal physical process—liquid being expelled from a syringe. The behavior of the droplets is consistent with well-understood principles of fluid dynamics and does not indicate any interaction with 5G networks. This post represents a common form of misinformation that seeks to link unrelated technologies and cause unwarranted concern about vaccine safety.

Video, ktoré sa šíri na sociálnych sieťach, tvrdí, že ukazuje výstup kvapalín z injekčnej stéky, pričom nadpis tvrdí, že vakcína v nej je manipulovaná alebo „pláva“ pomocou technológie 5G. Vzostupujúce správy tvrdia, že 5G siete niekým spôsobujú interakciu s obsahom vakcíny, čo viedlo k pozorovanému chovaniu kvapaliny v stéke.

**Pozadie a kontext**

Od začiatku pandémie COVID-19 sa na internete šíril nepravdivý informácie o vakcínách. Medzi najtrvajúcimi teóriami spochybnenia sú tie, ktoré sa týkajú mobilných sietí 5G. Niektoré z týchto tvrdení nesprávne tvrdia, že technológia 5G môže interagovať s vakcínami proti ochoreniu COVID-19, buď tým, že aktivuje „mikročipy“ prítomné v vakcíne, alebo tým, že mení ich fyzikálne vlastnosti. Tieto tvrdenia boli viackrát odmietnuté zdravotníckymi expertmi a výskumníkmi, ale stále sa šíria v niektorých online komunitách.

**Analýza obsahu videa**

Vzorové video zobrazuje záber injekčnej stéky, kde sa kvapaliny vylučujú z jej konca. Nie je vidieť žiadna vonkajšia zariadenie alebo technológia, okrem ruky, ktorá pohybuje stékom. Nadpis však tvrdí, že technológia 5G je zodpovedná za chovanie kvapaliny, čo implikuje, že elektromagnetické vlny z 5G vysielačov alebo zariadení spôsobujú, aby vakcína (alebo v tomto prípade voda) „plávala“ alebo sa chovala nezvyčajne.

Na analýzu tohto tvrdenia je dôležité pochopiť, ako fungujú injekčné stéky a technológia 5G:

- **Injekčné stéky:** Keď sa na páčku stéky pôsobí tlak, vytlačí sa kvapalina cez jehlu alebo otvor. Vytváranie kvapalín na konci je normálny fyzikálny jav spôsobený povrchovým napätím a vlastnosťami kvapaliny. Tento jav nastáva bez ohľadu na typ kvapaliny alebo prítomnosť elektromagnetických polí.
  
- **Technológia 5G:** 5G je piate generácie mobilných sietí. Funguje vysielaním rádiových vln (RF), podobne ako predchádzajúce generácie (4G, 3G). Tieto vlny sú neionizujúce a nemôžu manipulovať s látkami na mikroskopickom alebo makroskopickom úrovni tak, ako to tvrdí video. Nie je známa žiadna vedecká mechanizmus, ktorý by mohol spôsobiť, aby kvapalina v stéke „plávala“ alebo sa chovala inak.

**Vedecký konsenzus**

Vedné a zdravotnícké inštitúcie opakované tvrdia, že rádiové vlny 5G nie sú schopné interagovať s obsahom vakcíny. Nie je žiadna dôkaz, že signály 5G môžu zmeniť fyzikálne vlastnosti surovín vakcíny alebo vplyvovať ich chovanie v akomkoľvek spôsobe. Video, ktoré ukazuje výstup kvapalín z injekčnej stéky, je ľahko vysvetliteľné základnou fyzikou a nevyžaduje použitie bezdrôtových technológií.

**Záver**

Tvrdenie, že technológia 5G spôsobuje, aby vakcína v stéke „plávala“ alebo bola manipulovaná, je nezákerné a nezaložené na žiadnom vedeckom dôkaze. Video jednoducho ukazuje normálny fyzikálny proces – výstup kvapaliny z injekčnej stéky. Chovanie kvapalín je v súlade s dobre poznávanými princípmi hydromechaniky a neukazuje žiadnu interakciu s 5G sietami. Tento príspevok predstavuje bežný tvar dezinformácií, ktorý sa snaží spojiť nepriamo súvisiace technológie a spôsobiť neopodstatnené obavy ohľadom bezpečnosti vakcíny.

In recent months, social media platforms have seen a surge in posts about the Delta variant of COVID-19, with one widely shared claim stating: “The Delta variant does not cause coughs and fever, because this variant travels directly to the lungs. It is far deadlier than other variants.” This statement has caused confusion and concern among the public, leading to questions about its accuracy and the actual characteristics of the Delta variant.

To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to understand what the Delta variant is and how it differs from other variants of the virus. The Delta variant, officially known as B.1.617.2, was first identified in India in late 2020 and rapidly became the dominant strain in many countries due to its high transmissibility. Like other variants, the Delta variant is a mutation of the original SARS-CoV-2 virus that causes COVID-19.

The claim makes two main assertions: first, that the Delta variant does not cause the typical symptoms of cough and fever because it travels “directly to the lungs,” and second, that it is “far deadlier” than other variants.

Starting with the first claim, clinical evidence does not support the notion that the Delta variant bypasses common upper respiratory symptoms such as cough and fever. In fact, studies and health authorities have observed that while the symptom profile of the Delta variant may differ slightly from previous strains, it still generally includes classic COVID-19 symptoms such as cough, fever, headache, and sore throat. Some reports have suggested that symptoms like runny nose and headache might be more prominent, especially among younger populations, but cough and fever remain common. There is no evidence that the Delta variant travels in a fundamentally different way through the body, nor that it directly targets the lungs to the exclusion of the upper respiratory tract.

The second assertion—that the Delta variant is “far deadlier”—also requires context. While the Delta variant is recognized for its increased transmissibility, evidence regarding its severity and mortality is more nuanced. Some studies showed a higher risk of hospitalization and severe illness compared to earlier variants, particularly among unvaccinated individuals. However, the risk of death also depends on a variety of factors, including age, underlying health conditions, and vaccination status. Calling Delta “far deadlier” than other variants oversimplifies the data and does not reflect the full range of scientific findings. Importantly, vaccines have been shown to significantly reduce the risk of severe disease and death from the Delta variant.

In summary, the social media claim misrepresents the clinical characteristics and risk profile of the Delta variant. The Delta variant can and does cause coughs and fever in many patients, and while it may be more transmissible and potentially associated with increased severity, it is not categorically “far deadlier” than all other variants. Public understanding is best supported by referring to up-to-date, evidence-based health information rather than viral social media posts.

In de afgelopen maanden zijn sociale media-platforms getroffen door een stijging van berichten over de Delta-variant van het coronavirus, met als veel gedeelde bewering: "De Delta-variant veroorzaakt geen hoest en koorts, omdat deze variant direct naar de longen gaat. Deze variant is veel dodelijker dan andere varianten." Deze uitspraak heeft tot verwarring en zorgen bij het publiek geleid, waardoor er vragen zijn opgekomen over de juistheid van deze bewering en de werkelijke kenmerken van de Delta-variant.

Om de geldigheid van deze bewering te beoordelen, is het belangrijk om te begrijpen wat de Delta-variant is en hoe deze zich verschilt van andere varianten van het virus. De Delta-variant, officieel bekend als B.1.617.2, werd eind 2020 voor het eerst in India ontdekt en is snel tot de dominerende variant geworden in vele landen door haar hoge overdraagbaarheid. Net als andere varianten is de Delta-variant een mutatie van het oorspronkelijke SARS-CoV-2-virus dat de ziekte COVID-19 veroorzaakt.

De bewering maakt twee belangrijke beweringen: ten eerste dat de Delta-variant geen typische symptomen zoals hoest en koorts veroorzaakt, omdat deze variant "rechtstreeks naar de longen gaat", en ten tweede dat deze variant "veel dodelijker" is dan andere varianten.

Begonnen met de eerste bewering, klinisch bewijs ondersteunt niet de aanname dat de Delta-variant de gebruikelijke bovenste ademhalingssymptomen zoals hoest en koorts omzeilt. In feite hebben studies en gezondheidsinstanties waargenomen dat de symptoomprofiel van de Delta-variant zich licht verschilt van vroegere varianten, maar dat het in het algemeen klassieke symptomen van het coronavirus bevat, zoals hoest, koorts, hoofdpijn en keelpijn. Sommige rapporten suggereren dat symptomen zoals een loopneus en hoofdpijn mogelijk meer opvallen, vooral bij jongere mensen, maar hoest en koorts blijven veelvoorkomend. Er is geen bewijs dat de Delta-variant op een fundamenteel andere manier door het lichaam gaat, noch dat deze direct de longen aantast en de bovenste ademhalingstrajecten over het hoofd ziet.

De tweede bewering – dat de Delta-variant "veel dodelijker" is – vereist ook context. Hoewel de Delta-variant bekend staat om haar verhoogde overdraagbaarheid, is het bewijs over haar ernst en overlijdensrisico meer geforceerd. Sommige studies toonden een hoger risico op ziekenhuisopname en ernstige ziekte vergeleken met vroeger varianten, vooral bij ongevaccineerde personen. Echter, het overlijdensrisico hangt ook af van een reeks factoren, waaronder leeftijd, onderliggende gezondheidsproblemen en vaccinatiestatus. De bewering dat Delta "veel dodelijker" is dan andere varianten vereenvoudigt de data en weerspiegelt niet de volledige reeks wetenschappelijke bevindingen. Belangrijk is dat vaccins zijn getoond om het risico op ernstige ziekte en overlijden aan de Delta-variant aanzienlijk te verminderen.

In korte, de sociale media-bewering vertoont een misverstand over de klinische kenmerken en het risicoprofiel van de Delta-variant.
